target_claim: The formula sqrt(a_1^2+a_2^2) defines a norm on C^2, in particular satisfying norm(x)=0 iff x=0.
source_quote:
We define a [[Definition:Norm on Vector Space|norm]] on $\left({\C^2, \times}\right)$ by:
:$\forall \mathbf a = \tuple {a_1, a_2} \in \C^2: \norm {\mathbf a} = \sqrt {a_1^2 + a_2^2}$

This is a [[Definition:Norm on Vector Space|norm]] because:

:$(1): \quad \norm {\mathbf x} = 0 \iff \mathbf x = \mathbf 0$
